answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence depends on paths from independently trusted nodes rather than raw identities. A sybil cluster isolated behind a sparse external cut has low conductance; mixing across its boundary is limited, bounding its aggregate voting weight relative to honest, well-connected volume. Even a spiral of mutually attesting accounts cannot cross that ledge without acquiring credible links beyond its tundra of sybils.
